quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The manager which approved my request left the company.'
quests.targetClause: The manager who approved my request left the company.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The manager which approved my request left the company.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Which' cannot refer to a person; 'who' correctly supplies the subject of 'approved.'
quests.nativeTip: The manager is a person - check which pronoun fits, and whether the clause still needs its subject.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The manager who approved my request left the company."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The photo, that I took last summer, won a prize.'
quests.targetClause: The photo, which I took last summer, won a prize.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The photo, that I took last summer, won a prize.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' can never follow a comma; since 'the photo' is a specific, already-identified photo, 'which' is the correct fix.
quests.nativeTip: One relative pronoun can never follow a comma - which one, and what should replace it?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The photo, which I took last summer, won a prize."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Antecedent Identification
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The bundle of documents that were signed yesterday is ready for filing.'
quests.targetClause: The bundle of documents that was signed yesterday is ready for filing.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The bundle of documents that were signed yesterday is ready for filing.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The bundle' - not 'documents' - is the true antecedent and is singular, so both verbs must be singular: 'was signed' and 'is ready.'
quests.nativeTip: Find the true antecedent of 'that were signed' - is it 'documents' or 'the bundle'? Then check that both verbs in the sentence agree with it.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The bundle of documents that was signed yesterday is ready for filing."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: That Cannot Introduce Non-Defining Clauses
quests.questionSentence: Each option below has a different kind of error. Which one is a PUNCTUATION error?
quests.targetClause: My father, that taught me to fish, passed away last spring.
quests.completedSentence: Each option below has a different kind of error. Which one is a PUNCTUATION error?
quests.ruleExplanation: Option A's error is specifically about punctuation: 'that' can never follow a comma, which makes it a punctuation-category error rather than a plain pronoun, adverb, or omission error.
quests.nativeTip: Punctuation errors specifically involve commas or the pronouns that are, or aren't, allowed to follow them.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "My father, that taught me to fish, passed away last spring."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Subject Relative Pronoun Cannot Be Omitted
quests.grammarRule: Subject Relative Pronoun Cannot Be Omitted
quests.questionSentence: Each option below has a different kind of error. Which one is an OMISSION error?
quests.targetClause: The employee missed the deadline apologized to the team.
quests.completedSentence: Each option below has a different kind of error. Which one is an OMISSION error?
quests.ruleExplanation: Option A's error is that the subject relative pronoun has been dropped even though the clause needs a subject - an omission error, distinct from the pronoun, adverb, and punctuation errors elsewhere.
quests.nativeTip: An omission error specifically involves a relative pronoun that has been left out when it shouldn't have been.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The employee missed the deadline apologized to the team."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Adverbs Cannot Be Subjects
quests.questionSentence: Each option below has a different kind of error. Which one is a relative ADVERB error?
quests.targetClause: The delay why frustrated every passenger was never explained.
quests.completedSentence: Each option below has a different kind of error. Which one is a relative ADVERB error?
quests.ruleExplanation: Option A misuses 'why' as the subject of 'frustrated,' something a relative adverb can never be - an adverb-category error, distinct from the others here.
quests.nativeTip: An adverb error mismatches place, time, or reason - or uses an adverb where only a pronoun can do the job.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The delay why frustrated every passenger was never explained."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Fix this line from a job posting: 'We are looking for a candidate which has strong communication skills.'
quests.targetClause: We are looking for a candidate who has strong communication skills.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this line from a job posting: 'We are looking for a candidate which has strong communication skills.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' correctly refers to a person and supplies the subject of 'has.'
quests.nativeTip: A candidate is a person - check which pronoun fits, and whether the clause still needs its subject.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "We are looking for a candidate who has strong communication skills."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Fix this line from an instruction manual: 'Remove the panel which covers the battery compartment, that is located on the back of the device.'
quests.targetClause: Remove the panel that covers the battery compartment, which is located on the back of the device.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this line from an instruction manual: 'Remove the panel which covers the battery compartment, that is located on the back of the device.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That covers the battery compartment' is defining, since there could be several panels, so it needs 'that' and no comma; 'which is located on the back' is non-defining extra detail, so it needs a comma and 'which.'
quests.nativeTip: There are two clauses here - one that identifies which panel, and one that adds extra location detail. Check punctuation and pronoun for each separately.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "Remove the panel that covers the battery compartment, which is located on the back of the device."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Fix this line from a recipe: 'Add the butter, that should be softened beforehand, to the bowl.'
quests.targetClause: Add the butter, which should be softened beforehand, to the bowl.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this line from a recipe: 'Add the butter, that should be softened beforehand, to the bowl.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' can never follow a comma; since there's only one butter being referred to, 'which' correctly introduces this non-defining detail.
quests.nativeTip: One specific relative pronoun is banned from ever following a comma - which is it, and what should replace it here?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "Add the butter, which should be softened beforehand, to the bowl."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Fronted Preposition in Academic Collocations
quests.questionSentence: Fix this line from a research abstract: 'This study examines the extent which social media affects adolescent sleep patterns.'
quests.targetClause: This study examines the extent to which social media affects adolescent sleep patterns.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this line from a research abstract: 'This study examines the extent which social media affects adolescent sleep patterns.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Extent' pairs with 'to,' and the preposition moves in front of 'which' in this fixed academic pattern: 'the extent to which.'
quests.nativeTip: The word 'extent' collocates with a specific preposition - which one, and where should it sit?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "This study examines the extent to which social media affects adolescent sleep patterns."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Fix this line from a report conclusion: 'The findings, that were presented at the conference, sparked considerable debate.'
quests.targetClause: The findings, which were presented at the conference, sparked considerable debate.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this line from a report conclusion: 'The findings, that were presented at the conference, sparked considerable debate.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That' can never follow a comma; 'which' correctly introduces this non-defining clause about the findings.
quests.nativeTip: This clause sits between two commas - which relative pronoun is not permitted to appear there?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The findings, which were presented at the conference, sparked considerable debate."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Quantifier + of + whom/which
quests.questionSentence: Fix this line from a study summary: 'The survey reached two thousand respondents, most of who reported high stress levels.'
quests.targetClause: The survey reached two thousand respondents, most of whom reported high stress levels.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this line from a study summary: 'The survey reached two thousand respondents, most of who reported high stress levels.'
quests.ruleExplanation: After a preposition, a person takes 'whom,' not 'who': 'most of whom reported high stress levels.'
quests.nativeTip: Check which pronoun is allowed directly after the preposition 'of' when the antecedent is a group of people.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The survey reached two thousand respondents, most of whom reported high stress levels."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Find the error in this dense sentence: 'The proposal that the committee, whose members represent five departments, ultimately approved will be implemented next quarter.'
quests.targetClause: There is no error; the sentence is correct.
quests.completedSentence: Find the error in this dense sentence: 'The proposal that the committee, whose members represent five departments, ultimately approved will be implemented next quarter.'
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence is actually correct: 'whose members represent five departments' is a properly punctuated non-defining clause about 'the committee,' and 'that the committee ... approved' is a correctly unpunctuated defining clause about 'the proposal.'
quests.nativeTip: Check the punctuation around 'whose members represent five departments' carefully, and check whether 'that' is being used correctly as a defining pronoun.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "There is no error; the sentence is correct."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Whose vs Who's Distinction
quests.questionSentence: Find the error in this sentence: 'The scientist who's research on renewable energy earned international recognition retired last year.'
quests.targetClause: 'Who's' should be 'whose,' since possession is intended, not a contraction of 'who is.'
quests.completedSentence: Find the error in this sentence: 'The scientist who's research on renewable energy earned international recognition retired last year.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who's' is a contraction of 'who is,' which does not fit here; possession is intended, so 'whose' is required.
quests.nativeTip: Read 'who's' out loud as its full form - does that full form make sense here?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "'Who's' should be 'whose,' since possession is intended, not a contraction of 'who is.'"

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Stranded Preposition in Relative Clauses
quests.questionSentence: Find the error in this sentence: 'The clinic in which my grandmother received treatment for over a decade in has since closed.'
quests.targetClause: The preposition 'in' appears twice - once before 'which' and once at the end of the clause.
quests.completedSentence: Find the error in this sentence: 'The clinic in which my grandmother received treatment for over a decade in has since closed.'
quests.ruleExplanation: The preposition 'in' appears twice, once fronted before 'which' and once stranded at the end; only one position should be used.
quests.nativeTip: Tally how many times the preposition shows up - it should appear in only one spot.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The preposition 'in' appears twice - once before 'which' and once at the end of the clause."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Which revision is both grammatically correct and the clearest way to express this idea: 'The email arrived late. The email contained the wrong attachment. This caused a delay in the project.'
quests.targetClause: The late email, which contained the wrong attachment, delayed the project.
quests.completedSentence: Which revision is both grammatically correct and the clearest way to express this idea: 'The email arrived late. The email contained the wrong attachment. This caused a delay in the project.'
quests.ruleExplanation: Turning 'arrived late' into the adjective 'late' and combining the remaining facts into one clean non-defining clause is both correct and the most efficient way to express all three original facts.
quests.nativeTip: Look for the version that packages the same information most efficiently, without sacrificing correct grammar.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The late email, which contained the wrong attachment, delayed the project."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Spoken vs Formal Preposition Placement
quests.questionSentence: Which revision is best for a friendly internal team update, not a formal external document?
quests.targetClause: The bug that our QA team identified yesterday has been resolved.
quests.completedSentence: Which revision is best for a friendly internal team update, not a formal external document?
quests.ruleExplanation: This version is clear, correctly punctuated, and appropriately professional-but-casual for an internal update; the alternative is needlessly formal and wordy for this audience.
quests.nativeTip: Match the level of formality to a casual, internal audience without breaking any grammar rules.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The bug that our QA team identified yesterday has been resolved."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Which Referring to an Entire Clause
quests.grammarRule: Which Referring to an Entire Clause
quests.questionSentence: Which revision most clearly removes the ambiguity in 'The coach criticized the strategy of the team captain, which upset several players'?
quests.targetClause: The coach's criticism of the team captain's strategy upset several players.
quests.completedSentence: Which revision most clearly removes the ambiguity in 'The coach criticized the strategy of the team captain, which upset several players'?
quests.ruleExplanation: Turning 'criticized' into the noun 'criticism' removes the ambiguity: it becomes clearly the coach's criticism, the whole event, that upset players, rather than leaving 'which' to possibly point to the strategy, the captain, or the act of criticizing.
quests.nativeTip: Look for the version that gives 'which' or its replacement just one specific, unambiguous thing to attach to.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The coach's criticism of the team captain's strategy upset several players."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The report prepare by the analyst contained several errors.'
quests.targetClause: The report prepared by the analyst contained several errors.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The report prepare by the analyst contained several errors.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Prepared' is the correct past participle, showing the report was prepared by the analyst.
quests.nativeTip: 'Prepare' is not a valid participle form here - which form correctly shows the report was prepared by someone else?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The report prepared by the analyst contained several errors."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The house who belonging to my uncle is for sale.'
quests.targetClause: The house belonging to my uncle is for sale.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The house who belonging to my uncle is for sale.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Belonging to my uncle' is a correct reduced clause on its own; keeping 'who' alongside it is never allowed.
quests.nativeTip: A reduced clause never keeps its relative pronoun - check which option removes it correctly.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The house belonging to my uncle is for sale."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Relative Clause with -ing
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'Mount Kilimanjaro standing at over 5,800 meters is the tallest peak in Africa.'
quests.targetClause: Mount Kilimanjaro, standing at over 5,800 meters, is the tallest peak in Africa.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'Mount Kilimanjaro standing at over 5,800 meters is the tallest peak in Africa.'
quests.ruleExplanation: Since Mount Kilimanjaro is unique, this reduced clause is non-defining and needs commas on both sides, even though it has no relative pronoun.
quests.nativeTip: Reducing a clause doesn't remove the need for its commas - check whether they need to be restored here.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "Mount Kilimanjaro, standing at over 5,800 meters, is the tallest peak in Africa."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Preposition + whom/which (Fronted Preposition)
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The colleague to who I report has been very supportive.'
quests.targetClause: The colleague to whom I report has been very supportive.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The colleague to who I report has been very supportive.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Who' can never follow a preposition; a person after a fronted preposition takes 'whom.'
quests.nativeTip: Check which pronoun is allowed to follow a preposition directly.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The colleague to whom I report has been very supportive."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Choosing the Correct Preposition in Relative Clauses
quests.grammarRule: Choosing the Correct Preposition in Relative Clauses
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The garden of which I spent countless hours in has finally bloomed.'
quests.targetClause: The garden in which I spent countless hours has finally bloomed.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The garden of which I spent countless hours in has finally bloomed.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Spend hours in' takes 'in,' not 'of'; the fronted preposition should be 'in which,' matching the verb it belongs to.
quests.nativeTip: Say the phrase as a normal sentence first: 'I spent countless hours ___ the garden.' Which preposition actually belongs there?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The garden in which I spent countless hours has finally bloomed."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Quantifier + of + whom/which
quests.questionSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The board consists of nine members, three of them are new this year.'
quests.targetClause: The board consists of nine members, three of whom are new this year.
quests.completedSentence: Fix this sentence: 'The board consists of nine members, three of them are new this year.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Three of whom' correctly fixes the comma splice by turning the second half into a proper non-defining relative clause about the members.
quests.nativeTip: Joining two complete clauses with only a comma is an error - which fix turns this into one properly connected clause?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The board consists of nine members, three of whom are new this year."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: That Cannot Introduce Non-Defining Clauses
quests.questionSentence: Read this passage: 'The clinic opened in 2010. The doctor who founded it retired last year. The staff, that she trained personally, now run daily operations. Patients who visit regularly praise the care they receive.' Which sentence contains an error?
quests.targetClause: The staff, that she trained personally, now run daily operations.
quests.completedSentence: Read this passage: 'The clinic opened in 2010. The doctor who founded it retired last year. The staff, that she trained personally, now run daily operations. Patients who visit regularly praise the care they receive.' Which sentence contains an error?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That she trained personally' incorrectly follows a comma; since the staff are already identified, this is non-defining and needs 'which' or 'whom,' never 'that.'
quests.nativeTip: Check each sentence's relative clause separately - especially any that follow a comma.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The staff, that she trained personally, now run daily operations."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Non-Defining Clauses Cannot Omit Their Pronoun
quests.grammarRule: Non-Defining Clauses Cannot Omit Their Pronoun
quests.questionSentence: Read this passage: 'Our team launched a new app last spring. The features we added were based on user feedback. The update, users have been requesting for months, finally arrived last week. Reviews have been overwhelmingly positive.' Which sentence contains an error?
quests.targetClause: The update, users have been requesting for months, finally arrived last week.
quests.completedSentence: Read this passage: 'Our team launched a new app last spring. The features we added were based on user feedback. The update, users have been requesting for months, finally arrived last week. Reviews have been overwhelmingly positive.' Which sentence contains an error?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The update, users have been requesting' drops the pronoun inside a non-defining clause, which is never allowed; it should read 'which users have been requesting.'
quests.nativeTip: Look specifically at sentences with commas - does the clause between them still have a visible connecting word?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The update, users have been requesting for months, finally arrived last week."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Relative Adverb of Reason (why)
quests.questionSentence: Read this passage: 'The factory closed after decades of operation. The reason when it closed was never made public. Former employees, whose pensions were affected, have filed a complaint. A hearing is scheduled for next month.' Which sentence contains an error?
quests.targetClause: The reason when it closed was never made public.
quests.completedSentence: Read this passage: 'The factory closed after decades of operation. The reason when it closed was never made public. Former employees, whose pensions were affected, have filed a complaint. A hearing is scheduled for next month.' Which sentence contains an error?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The reason when it closed' incorrectly pairs 'when' with 'the reason'; it should be 'the reason why it closed,' since 'why' is the relative adverb of reason.
quests.nativeTip: Check each relative word against its antecedent's category - place, time, reason, or person.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The reason when it closed was never made public."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Which sentence contains absolutely no errors?
quests.targetClause: The policy that the board approved unanimously takes effect next month.
quests.completedSentence: Which sentence contains absolutely no errors?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The policy that the board approved unanimously takes effect next month' is a correctly punctuated defining clause with the correct object pronoun; the other options each break a different rule.
quests.nativeTip: Check pronoun choice after 'of,' comma placement, and whether any clause has a stray comma or a wrongly dropped pronoun.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [defining] ➔ "The policy that the board approved unanimously takes effect next month."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Reduced Passive Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Which of these four sentences has zero grammatical errors?
quests.targetClause: The village in which the festival, held every August, takes place is tiny.
quests.completedSentence: Which of these four sentences has zero grammatical errors?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In which the festival, held every August, takes place' correctly fronts the preposition and properly punctuates the non-defining reduced clause; the other options each contain an invalid form or misplaced preposition.
quests.nativeTip: Check the preposition placement, the reduced clause's punctuation, and the participle forms across all four options.
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The village in which the festival, held every August, takes place is tiny."

quests.conceptTitle: Information Snap-In: Defining vs Non-Defining Relative Clause
quests.questionSentence: Out of these four, which sentence is fully correct?
quests.targetClause: The witness whom the defense recalled, who had testified earlier that week, changed key details of her account.
quests.completedSentence: Out of these four, which sentence is fully correct?
quests.ruleExplanation: This option correctly stacks a defining clause ('whom the defense recalled') with a non-defining one ('who had testified earlier that week'), with accurate punctuation and pronoun choice throughout.
quests.nativeTip: Check each clause separately: is it defining or non-defining, does the punctuation match, and does each pronoun fit its grammatical role?
quests.legoPreview: 🧩 Snap Slot: [non-defining] ➔ "The witness whom the defense recalled, who had testified earlier that week, changed key details of her account."
